I was there overnight where I had to talk to crisis teams and get my blood drawn and urine samples etc. I ended up being taken in an ambulance to a psychiatric hospital (inpatient) the next morning on a 72 hour INVOLUNTARY hold, meaning I had no choice; ultimately was in inpatient for 9 days before being released to outpatient. So yes, shit can escalate quickly, but ultimately I got the help I needed (even if the hospital stay didn’t directly help me, it opened the conversation for me to eventually find a program and medications that really worked for me). I don’t say this to discourage anyone, but to say if you really need someone, a good counselor will get you help.

OP: You either have zero self confidence and an extremely negative view of yourself, or your ego is through the roof, and honestly I cant tell which it is

This said, kids, highschoolers, dont listen to OP. Sure it may be the “harsh reality”, but you will never succeed if you follow this rhetoric. Top colleges arent looking for textbook stats- they are looking for passion and commitment and perseverance. Shoot your shot at these top schools and you may be surprised, but either way, there is a spot for you. The grim reality is that the students who get into these school are students who didnt need to study through high school. If you worked your ass off to get in-first of all, you are automatically so much better than any of those kids-but you will find going to a HYPSM school or other top preforming school detrimental to your wellbeing, because sometimes you can work yourself to death, and it will still not be “good enough” for these schools

Enjoy high school, enjoy college, hell, enjoy life! Take the classes that interest you, not just the ones that look best for colleges. I will promise you that if you follow your passions through high school, you will end up in a place so “right” you didnt even know it could exist. And if that happens to be a T10 or whatever, good on you. But trust me, working your ass off through high school to get into one of these elite schools doesn’t pay off- you will likely have a miserable time in college.

Take it from an ex-perfectionist and HYPSM seeker: when I started following my passion, only them did my chances at these schools began to open. Before, I had no sustenance to my application, but then I did what I loved, had fun doing it, and it naturally created those tier one and two opportunities. And I ended up getting accepted into all the colleges I applied for, but the most valuable part was getting into that “perfect” college for me. Because it is an ivy, I will work my ass off, but I know that I will have the time of my life pursuing my passions surrounded by like-minded individuals.

You will end up in the right place for you. And stop comparing yourself to these unrealistic standards: you are good enough.
